corpus.title: Moscow says Britain will ‘have to answer’ for the UK-made drones hitting Russian refineries
corpus.signal_text:
Moscow says Britain will ‘have to answer’ for the UK-made drones hitting Russian refineries
The Russian Embassy in London has accused the United Kingdom of “deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis” after news reports said British-made drones had been used in strikes deep inside Russia.
“London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” the embassy said in a statement. “The deeper its involvement in the conflict and the greater its support for Kyiv’s terrorist machine, the higher the price it will pay for this.”
The embassy did not specify exactly what “consequences” the United Kingdom should expect. Russia has threatened Britain before over British deliveries of Storm Shadow missiles and drone-manufacturing technology to Ukraine.
Britain’s Defense Ministry told the BBC that the country stands “shoulder to shoulder” with Ukraine. “We are committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against Putin’s illegal invasion,” a ministry representative said.
On August 16, The Sunday Times first reported the use of British drones in long-range strikes. According to the newspaper, Ukraine has recently received two types of drones from the United Kingdom: one with a range of about 150 miles (240 kilometers), the other about 600 miles (960 kilometers).
The newspaper said the drones were used in this summer’s campaign of long-range strikes on Russian territory, including attacks on oil refineries and warehouses belonging to the Russian online retailer Wildberries. A well-placed military source later confirmed to the BBC that British drones had been used.
Britain’s Defense Ministry first said in April that it would send long-range strike drones to Ukraine, as part of an aid package worth 500 million pounds — the largest such package since the start of the war. The package reportedly included more than 150,000 drones.
The war in photos: Pechenihy, Ukraine’s Kharkiv region
Russian forces carried out a missile strike on the village of Pechenihy in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region on Tuesday morning, hitting a crowded intersection where a post office, stores, and homes stand. Ukrainian authorities said 10 people were killed and 17 injured. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine “will certainly respond to this Russian strike.”

corpus.title: Drone Attack Near Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant Kills One, IAEA Says
corpus.signal_text:
The UN's nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency, said Tuesday that a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one and injuring several others.
In a post on X, the IAEA, citing the plant's director, said the explosion took place around 6 a.m. local time.
"The explosion caused 16 casualties among staff and subcontractors, including one death and three serious injuries," the agency said.
The plant's director described the incident as "the worst event the plant has faced," the IAEA added.
It was not immediately clear whether the drone was Russian or Ukrainian.
Russian forces seized the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, Europe's largest with six reactors, in the first weeks of the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Both Russia and Ukraine regularly accuse each other of risking nuclear disaster at the plant.
IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi on Tuesday called on "military commanders responsible for these actions as well as all others aiming [at] nuclear power plants and/or their staff to put an immediate stop to these unacceptable actions."
They "constitute great risks to nuclear safety and security during the conflict," Grossi added.

Air defense forces shoot down 56 drones and two Banderole drones launched by Russia against Ukraine overnight
According to Ukrinform, the Ukrainian Air Force reported this on Telegram.
According to military sources, starting at 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday, August 18, the enemy launched an attack using two “Iskander-M” ballistic missiles, 65 Shahed-type strike UAVs (including jet-powered ones), “Gerbera,” ‘Banderole’ loitering munitions, and “Parody”-type decoy drones from the following directions: Kursk, Orel, as well as the temporarily occupied Donetsk and Hvardiyske (in the temporarily occupied Crimea).
The air attack was repelled by the Ukrainian Air Force, anti-aircraft missile forces, electronic warfare units, unmanned systems, and mobile fire groups of the Ukrainian Defense Forces.
According to preliminary data, as of 8:30 a.m. on Wednesday, August 19, air defense forces shot down or neutralized 56 drones and two “Banderole” drones in northern, southern, and eastern Ukraine.
Hits were recorded at 10 locations, and downed targets (debris) were found at three locations.
The attack is ongoing, with several enemy drones in the airspace.
As reported by Ukrinform, on August 18, Russian troops launched a missile strike on Pechenihy in the Kharkiv region, killing 10 people.
